text: 4.d3: off goes the pawn on d2, forward from d2 to d3. The pawn on d3 now guards the bishop on c4. The bishop on c1, stuck until now, is free after 4.d3. Meanwhile Black's knight on f6 already has White's queen on h5 in its sights. After 4.d3, nobody looks after the queen on h5 any more. 4...Nxh5: Black's knight on f6 takes the queen on h5. White could have played 4.Qxf7# instead of 4.d3. 4.Qxf7#: White's queen on h5 takes the pawn on f7. 4.Qxf7# gives check to the king on e8, and it is mate: the game ends, and White wins.

1.Qf7 sends the queen on f1 forward from f1 to f7. 1.Qf7, and it is stalemate: Black has no legal move and is not in check, so the game ends at once as a draw. What about 1.Qf8#? White could have played it instead of 1.Qf7. 1.Qf8#: off goes White's queen on f1, forward from f1 to f8. 1.Qf8# gives check to the king on h8, and it is mate: the game ends, and White wins.

1.Kg2 sends the king on g1 forward from g1 to g2. Black's knight on e5 cannot move, because the rook on e1 pins the knight on e5 to the king on e8. With 1...Kd7, Black's king on e8 sets off forward, from e8 to d7. What about 1.f4? White could have played it instead of 1.Kg2. 1.f4: off goes White's pawn on f2, forward from f2 to f4. The pawn on f4 attacks the knight on e5.

1.Qc1: the queen on d1 goes sideways from d1 to c1. 1...Ne2+ sends Black's knight on d4 forward from d4 to e2. The knight on e2 gives check to the king on g1. First 1...Ne2+ gives check; then, after the king moves, the knight on e2 takes the queen on c1 with 2...Nxc1. White could have played 1.Qxd4 instead of 1.Qc1. 1.Qxd4: White's queen on d1 grabs the knight on d4!

1...c5: the pawn on c7 goes forward from c7 to c5. 1...c5 lets the queen on d8 out: it could not move before. The bishop on f8 was already shut in by the pawns on e7 and g7 before 1...c5, and 1...c5 does not free it. 2.Nf3 sends White's knight on g1 forward from g1 to f3. Black could have played 1...e5 instead of 1...c5. With 1...e5, Black's pawn on e7 sets off forward, from e7 to e5. 1...e5 frees the bishop on f8.

2...Nf6: off goes the knight on g8, forward from g8 to f6. 2...Nf6 frees the rook on h8: it could not move before. 2...Nf6 does not free the bishop on c8: it was already shut in by the pawns on b7 and d7 before, and still is. 3.e5: White's pawn on e4 goes forward from e4 to e5. And the pawn on e5 has the knight on f6 in its sights. Instead of 2...Nf6, Black could have played 2...d6. 2...d6 sends Black's pawn on d7 forward from d7 to d6. 2...d6 would also let the bishop on c8 out.

3.e5: off goes the pawn on e4, forward from e4 to e5. The pawn on e5 attacks the knight on f6. With 3...Nd5, Black's knight on f6 sets off forward, from f6 to d5.

With 6...d6, the pawn on d7 sets off forward, from d7 to d6. 6...d6 frees the bishop on c8: it could not move before. 7.Bf4: White's bishop on c1 goes forward from c1 to f4. Instead of 6...d6, Black could have played 6...a6. 6...a6 sends Black's pawn on a7 forward from a7 to a6.

With 7...dxe5, the pawn on d6 helps itself to the pawn on e5. The pawn on e5 goes hunting for the bishop on f4. 8.Qxd8+: White's queen on d1 grabs the queen on d8! The queen on d8 calls check on the king on e8.

10...a6: the pawn on a7 goes forward from a7 to a6. 11.Bc7: off goes White's bishop on e5, forward from e5 to c7. 10...Bd7 was there for Black instead of 10...a6. With 10...Bd7, Black's bishop on c8 sets off forward, from c8 to d7.

With 16.c4, the pawn on c3 sets off forward, from c3 to c4. 16...h5: off goes Black's pawn on h7, forward from h7 to h5. What about 16.O-O? White could have played it instead of 16.c4. White castles kingside with 16.O-O; the king now stands on g1.
20.Rhd1: the rook on h1 goes sideways from h1 to d1. The rook on d1 defends the rook on d7. 20...Ke6 sends Black's king on f7 forward from f7 to e6. The king on e6 goes hunting for the rook on d7.

With 21...Bd6, the bishop on e7 sets off forward, from e7 to d6. 22.Ba5: White's bishop on b6 goes back from b6 to a5. What about 21...h5? Black could have played it instead of 21...Bd6. 21...h5 sends Black's pawn on h7 forward from h7 to h5.

22...Rc6: the rook on c8 goes forward from c8 to c6. White's rook on b7 already attacks Black's pawn on g7. After 22...Rc6, nobody looks after the pawn on g7 any more. 23.Rxg7: White's rook on b7 takes the pawn on g7. Black could have played 22...g6 instead of 22...Rc6. 22...g6 sends Black's pawn on g7 forward from g7 to g6.

With 13.Bg5, the bishop on c1 sets off forward, from c1 to g5. The bishop on g5 attacks the knight on f6. 13...Rd8: off goes Black's rook on c8, sideways from c8 to d8.

14...Qxf6: the queen on e7 grabs the bishop on f6! The queen on f6 attacks the knight on c3. White's knight on c3 already attacks Black's pawn on d5. 15.Nxd5, and White's knight on c3 snaps up the pawn on d5. And the knight on d5 has the queen on f6 in its sights. What about 14...gxf6? Black could have played it instead of 14...Qxf6. With 14...gxf6, Black's pawn on g7 helps itself to the bishop on f6.

15...Qh6 sends the queen on f6 sideways from f6 to h6. The queen on h6 attacks the bishop on h3. 16.Kg2: White's king on g1 steps forward from g1 to g2. The king on g2 defends the bishop on h3. 15...Bxf2+ was there for Black instead of 15...Qh6. With 15...Bxf2+, Black's bishop on c5 helps itself to the pawn on f2. The bishop on f2 gives check to the king on g1.

17.Qc1: off goes the queen on d1, sideways from d1 to c1. The queen on c1 attacks the bishop on c5. The queen on c1 now eyes the queen on h6. 17...exd5, and Black's pawn on e6 snaps up the knight on d5.

17.Qc1: off goes the queen on d1, sideways from d1 to c1. The queen on c1 attacks the bishop on c5. The queen on c1 now eyes the queen on h6. 17...exd5, and Black's pawn on e6 snaps up the knight on d5.
17...exd5: the pawn on e6 takes the knight on d5. 18.Qxc5, and White's queen on c1 snaps up the bishop on c5. And the queen on c5 has the knight on c6 in its sights.

With 20.Qd3, the queen on b5 sets off back, from b5 to d3. The queen on d3 attacks the queen on d2. The queen on d3 now eyes the knight on d4. Now Black's queen on d2 has White's queen on d3 in its sights. 20...Qxd3: Black's queen on d2 takes the queen on d3. The queen on d3 now guards the knight on d4. Instead of 20.Qd3, White could have played 20.Qa4. 20.Qa4: off goes White's queen on b5, back from b5 to a4. The queen on a4 goes hunting for the knight on d4.

22.Bg4 sends the bishop on h3 forward from h3 to g4. Now the king on g2 can step to h3. With 22...Kf7, Black's king on g8 sets off forward, from g8 to f7. 22.Rfe1 was there for White instead of 22.Bg4. 22.Rfe1: off goes White's rook on f1, sideways from f1 to e1. The rook on e1 now eyes the rook on e8.

24...Rb6: the rook on d6 goes sideways from d6 to b6. 25.Re5: off goes White's rook on e1, forward from e1 to e5. Black could have played 24...Kf7 instead of 24...Rb6. 24...Kf7 sends Black's king on g8 forward from g8 to f7.

30...a6 sends the pawn on a7 forward from a7 to a6. With 31.Rf7+, White's rook on f5 sets off forward, from f5 to f7. The rook on f7 calls check on the king on d7. First 31.Rf7+ gives check; then, after the king moves, the rook on f7 takes the pawn on g7 with 32.Rxg7. Black could have played 30...Kd6 instead of 30...a6. 30...Kd6: Black's king on d7 steps forward from d7 to d6.

38...b3: the pawn on b4 goes forward from b4 to b3. White's pawn on a2 attacks Black's pawn on b3. With 39.axb3, White's pawn on a2 helps itself to the pawn on b3. What about 38...Rxa2? Black could have played it instead of 38...b3. 38...Rxa2, and Black's rook on b2 snaps up the pawn on a2.
40.Bxc6: the bishop on d5 grabs the knight on c6! With 40...Kxc6, Black's king on b6 helps itself to the bishop on c6.
